messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we prototyped per-token confidence routing (decide at token time whether to emit in low-bit or re-run in fp16) and ran into two surprises. First, cost variance spiked on chatty prompts. Second, KV cache reuse gets messy when tokens are regenerated in a different precision.

sam: Curious — do you have the numbers? Was the cost mostly from re-runs or from extra memory pressure? :thinking_face:

maya: Mostly re-runs. We measured a 2.3x tail for 95th percentile cost on long conversations when threshold was 0.6. Average cost went up ~20% but latency SLO was violated <1% of requests (canary).

joel: That matches my intuition. Token-level fallback invalidates the cache for subsequent tokens if we don't carefully stitch. If token i is regenerated at fp16, the model kv for tokens <i might be incompatible because attention keys/values differ slightly. We hit divergence after ~8 tokens in the worst case.

lina: Right — and for embeddings/semantic search cases, one regenerated token can change the embedding and force downstream re-embeds if you're doing incremental embedding pipelines. That amplifies cost.

maya: Notes from the prototype:

```
precision_routing:
  per_token_window: 8
  confidence_threshold: 0.65
  fallback_mode: rerun-in-fp16
  stitch_strategy: strict-verify
```

We tried `stitch_strategy: strict-verify` which re-runs all subsequent tokens under fp16 if any mismatch is detected. That kept semantics but multiplied reruns.

sam: Two high-level options I see: (A) coarse-grained routing (per-chunk/per-turn) to avoid cache churn, or (B) keep token-level routing but only allow fallbacks that are cache-compatible (e.g., quant-consistent reruns or corrective deltas). Both have tradeoffs.

joel: For (B) we could implement a "compatibility mode" where fallback uses the same KV layout and quant scheme but runs a higher-precision math path (mixed-precision compute, not full fp16 model graph). That reduces divergence but is more work in runtime.

lina: Another pragmatic approach: limit token-level reruns to name-entity / short spans where change space is small. Use a small classifier that signals whether correction will cascade.

maya: I sketched a hybrid policy: chunk-level default + token-level exception for high-impact tokens. Policy config example: 

```
precision_policy:
  default_scope: chunk
  token_exceptions:
    enabled: true
    classifier_model: rwd/qa-token-impact-v1
    max_window: 6
```

This kept cache reuse 92% of the time and reduced cost spikes (95th cost tail down to 1.3x). Latency SLOs still held because exceptions were rare.

sam: Sounds promising. We need to consider telemetry too — we should emit per-request traces that tag when a token exception happened and whether it triggered cascade reruns. Without that we'll miss root causes.

infra-bot: deploy-status: canary/precision-routing-proto -> success (2024-11-12T14:03:12Z). Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/2140005678

joel: One more low-level detail: KV cache checksum idea — on rerun we compute a small checksum of kv slices and if checksum matches, allow using cached suffix. If mismatch, fall back to chunk-level rerun. Cheap and reduces wasted reruns.

lina: I like checksum + classifier combo. Checksum avoids expensive diff of kv tensors. Need to be careful about floating nondeterminism across devices. Use an integer hash of quantized kv.

maya: Action items:
- lina: prototype token-impact classifier thresholding and collect precision-cost traces (due EOW)
- joel: implement small kv-checksum shim in runtime (PR draft by next week)
- sam: update RFC with hybrid policy and telemetry requirements
- maya: run a 48h canary with mixed chat and embed workloads and share numbers

sam: +1. Also add cost guard rails in the console: dynamic alert if per-request token rerun rate > 2% for a cohort.

lina: Will add metric. Also will dump a few example threads where reruns changed user-visible output.

maya: Thanks all — we should avoid token-level sensitivity as a default but keep it as an opt-in with strong telemetry and fail-safes. :white_check_mark:
